case_name: Kyles v. Celadon Trucking Services, Inc.
argument: Plaintiff challenged Bain's biomechanical and spinal-injury qualifications and characterized his injury-causation analysis as unreliable.
opposition: The defense maintained Bain was qualified and had applied injury-causation analysis to adequate case information (as described in the order).
court_reasoning: The court accepted Bain's qualifications and found a sufficiently reliable basis for his injury-causation opinions.
scope_note: The order summarizes the arguments; the underlying motion and response briefs are not included in this dataset.

case_name: Kyles v. Celadon Trucking Services, Inc.
issue: Trucking safety expertise and sleep-apnea opinions
argument: Plaintiff argued a trucking safety consultant was not qualified to address sleep apnea and had no reliable basis to discuss treatment and its relation to the collision.
opposition: Defense distinguished motor-carrier safety and operational knowledge from medical expert testimony (as described in the order).
court_reasoning: The court treated the challenged opinions as specialized knowledge grounded in motor-carrier regulations and safety practice, not as medical diagnosis.
scope_note: The order summarizes the arguments; the underlying motion and response briefs are not included in this dataset.

case_name: Kyles v. Celadon Trucking Services, Inc.
issue: Crash severity and witness credibility opinions
argument: Plaintiff sought to exclude the spine surgeon's comments about crash severity and his characterization of the plaintiff as malingering or exaggerating.
opposition: The order describes Knox's examination findings, including Waddell signs; the underlying response brief is not included.
court_reasoning: The court excluded crash-severity and negative credibility characterizations, but allowed the doctor to describe clinical observations and inconsistency with objective tests.
scope_note: Grant concerned specified opinion categories, not wholesale exclusion of all medical testimony.

case_name: Kyles v. Celadon Trucking Services, Inc.
issue: Crash-severity assessment versus medical work-capacity opinion
argument: Defendants challenged a physician's characterization of collision severity and disputed the reliability of his opinions about the plaintiff's capacity to drive trucks.
opposition: The order discusses the physician's review of medical records and physical examination; original motion briefing is not included.
court_reasoning: The physician could testify regarding medical work capacity but not characterize the severity of the truck collision.
scope_note: Partial exclusion applied to crash severity, not the full work-capacity opinion.

issue: Engineering qualifications and chemical exposure testimony
argument: Defendant disputed whether the engineer's background supported testimony about the care expected from a nitric-acid manufacturer and specific medical injuries.
opposition: Plaintiffs defended her broader engineering safety analysis and contested the absence of some start-up data (as characterized by the court).
court_reasoning: The court permitted opinions within the expert's engineering scope, required narrower standard-of-care language, and prohibited testimony about the plaintiff's specific injuries.
scope_note: Partial exclusion; most of the engineer's analysis remained admissible.

argument: Defendant contended the treating pulmonologist's differential-causation method and exposure assumptions were unreliable.
opposition: Plaintiffs relied on treatment history and evidence supporting chemical exposure, as addressed in the opinion.
court_reasoning: The court allowed Sevin's medical causation testimony, including use of the assumed exposure as a premise the jury could evaluate.
scope_note: Court concluded the causation opinion was admissible; this is not a finding that the exposure fact was definitively proven.

argument: Defendant challenged the reliability of the physician's opinion that the exposure caused the plaintiff's pulmonary condition.
opposition: The court compared this opinion with the other physician's differential diagnosis; original response brief not available in the dataset.
court_reasoning: The court excluded the pulmonary-causation opinion because the expert did not adequately consider and rule out other plausible causes.
scope_note: Only the opinion on causation of pulmonary conditions was excluded; other opinions were not decided in this ruling.

case_name: Deflecto, LLC v. Dundas Jafine Inc.
issue: Patent damages, methodology, and transition damages
argument: Defendant advanced several challenges to the damages expert, including his handling of damages start dates, lost profits, and future or transition damages.
opposition: The order addresses the proposed damages methodologies; the challenged motion was identified as sealed.
court_reasoning: Most disagreements affected the weight of the testimony, but the expert's transition-damages opinion was excluded for lack of an identified legal basis.
scope_note: The underlying motion was sealed; only the public court order is part of this POC.

issue: Economic loss expert versus vocational and medical causation
argument: Defendants argued that an accountant was unqualified to address matters related to lost earning capacity without vocational expertise.
opposition: Plaintiff distinguished calculation of earnings from vocational and causation opinions.
court_reasoning: The court allowed lost-earnings calculations within the CPA's field while indicating vocational and causation opinions were outside that testimony.
scope_note: The order restricts the kind of testimony allowed even though the motion was denied.

issue: Accident reconstruction versus medical injury diagnosis
argument: Defendants argued the accident-reconstruction witness lacked sufficient expertise for collision biomechanics and could not provide medical opinions on injuries.
opposition: The order references Bourdage's experience and methods; the original response brief is not included.
court_reasoning: The court permitted reconstruction and general injury-mechanism analysis but barred testimony diagnosing which injuries the plaintiff actually sustained.
scope_note: The motion was denied, but the order expressly limited medical-injury testimony.
